title: 2.3. Variables: Data Containers & Identifiers
summary: Learn how variables act as named labels pointing to memory objects, variable naming rules (PEP 8), assignment (=), and shortcut compound assignment operators.
learningObjectives: Understand variable instantiation through assignment (=) without explicit type declarations.
Adhere to Python variable naming rules: letters, digits, underscores, case-sensitivity, and reserved keyword prohibitions.

sections.heading: 2.3.1 Naming Rules for Python Identifiers
sections.content:
A variable name (identifier) in Python must follow strict syntactic rules:
• Must begin with an uppercase/lowercase letter or an underscore (_). It CANNOT begin with a digit.
• Can only contain alphanumeric characters and underscores (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, _).
• Python is strictly case-sensitive: count, Count, and COUNT are three distinct variables.
• Cannot match any Python reserved keywords (e.g., if, for, while, class, def, return, import).

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Which of the following is an invalid variable identifier in Python?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Variable names in Python cannot begin with a numeric digit.

recap: Variables are dynamic memory labels. Identifiers cannot start with digits or use reserved keywords.
